title: Why Does Toast Burn After the Timer Lights Off?
alternate_titles: When the Green Light Fails: Toast Turns Black
The Hidden Heat That Char Your Bread
description: Why does toast burn even when the timer says 'done'? Every morning, we pull a golden slice only to find a black edge after the green light goes off. Understanding this mystery matters because it explains why our breakfast can turn from perfect to ruined in seconds. The culprit is the toaster’s residual heat: the nichrome element stays hot for 1–2 seconds after the circuit opens, continuing to radiate infrared energy that pushes the Maillard reaction past its sweet spot into caramelization and pyrolysis. Sources: Frigidaire support article on why some breads burn more easily; NZASE “Science of Toasters”; HowStuffWorks “How Toasters Work”.
